content.goal: This repository provides a curated collection of example plugins for Codex, demonstrating how developers can build plugin bundles for tools such as Figma, Notion, SwiftUI-based iOS/macOS apps, web apps, Expo, Netlify, Remotion, and Google Slides.
content.usage: Each plugin is organized under plugins/<name>/ and must include a .codex-plugin/plugin.json manifest, with optional companion files like skills/, .app.json, .mcp.json, agents/, commands/, hooks.json, and assets/. The default marketplace configuration is located at .agents/plugins/marketplace.json, pointing to the plugins/ directory.
content.pros: The repository offers several richer, real-world examples spanning design (Figma), knowledge work (Notion), mobile/desktop development (build-ios-apps, build-macos-apps, expo), and web deployment (build-web-apps, netlify), giving developers multiple reference implementations for learning plugin structure.
content.cons: Users authenticating with an API key appear to rely on a separate marketplace file (.agents/plugins/api_marketplace.json) rather than the default one, which suggests the plugin discovery setup may differ depending on login method and could require additional configuration awareness.
content.fit: This repository appears best suited for developers already working within the Codex ecosystem who want reference examples for building or extending plugins across design, productivity, and app-development domains, rather than for those seeking a single standalone tool.

content.goal: ECC is an MIT-licensed open-source "agent harness operating system" that adds a structured engineering workflow (plan, test, implement, review, verify, remember, improve) on top of AI coding agents. It ships 68 agents, 292 skills, and 94 legacy command shims, plus hooks, rules, memory, and AgentShield security scanning, and works primarily with Claude Code.
content.usage: The recommended install runs `npx ecc-universal@2.2.1 setup` for guided Claude Code plugin setup, or natively inside Claude Code via `/plugin marketplace add https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC` followed by `/plugin install ecc@ecc`. Only one install method should be used per harness to avoid duplicated skills, commands, or hooks.
content.pros: ECC bundles a large, pre-built catalog (68 agents, 292 skills) covering planning, TDD, code review, build repair, security, and domain-specific workflows, so teams do not need to assemble this tooling from scratch. It also includes AgentShield scanning for prompts, hooks, MCP configs, and secrets, and supports self-hosted or custom model endpoints without changing ECC's workflows.
content.cons: The README states ECC "works best with Claude Code today" and that adapters for other harnesses (Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, Zed, Copilot, and others) are "capability-limited," so full feature parity across harnesses is not guaranteed and should be checked before assuming equivalent behavior. Setup also requires Node.js 18+, and Claude plugin setup additionally requires Git and Claude Code 2.1+.
content.fit: ECC appears best suited for teams already standardized on Claude Code who want a structured, tool-assisted development workflow with reusable skills and security scanning. Teams relying primarily on other harnesses may get a reduced feature set, since the documented platform support table lists several integrations as beta, experimental, or instruction-only rather than at full parity.

es.goal: ECC es un "sistema operativo de arneses de agentes" de código abierto con licencia MIT que añade un flujo de trabajo de ingeniería estructurado (planificar, probar, implementar, revisar, verificar, recordar, mejorar) sobre agentes de codificación con IA. Incluye 68 agentes, 292 habilidades y 94 comandos heredados, además de hooks, reglas, memoria y escaneo de seguridad AgentShield, y funciona principalmente con Claude Code.
es.usage: La instalación recomendada es ejecutar `npx ecc-universal@2.2.1 setup` para la configuración guiada del plugin de Claude Code, o de forma nativa dentro de Claude Code mediante `/plugin marketplace add https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC` seguido de `/plugin install ecc@ecc`. Solo debe usarse un método de instalación por cada arnés para evitar duplicar habilidades, comandos o hooks.
es.pros: ECC incluye un amplio catálogo preconstruido (68 agentes, 292 habilidades) que cubre planificación, TDD, revisión de código, reparación de compilaciones, seguridad y flujos específicos de dominio, por lo que los equipos no necesitan ensamblar estas herramientas desde cero. También incorpora el escaneo AgentShield para prompts, hooks, configuraciones MCP y secretos, y admite endpoints de modelos autoalojados o personalizados sin cambiar los flujos de trabajo de ECC.

La instalación también requiere Node.js 18 o superior, y la configuración del plugin de Claude requiere además Git y Claude Code 2.1 o superior.
es.fit: ECC parece más adecuado para equipos que ya utilizan Claude Code como estándar y desean un flujo de desarrollo estructurado y asistido por herramientas con habilidades reutilizables y escaneo de seguridad. Los equipos que dependen principalmente de otros arneses podrían obtener un conjunto de funciones reducido, ya que la tabla de soporte de plataformas documentada clasifica varias integraciones como beta, experimentales o solo de instrucciones, en lugar de paridad completa.

ja.pros: ECCは計画、TDD、コードレビュー、ビルド修復、セキュリティ、ドメイン固有のワークフローをカバーする大規模な構築済みカタログ(68エージェント、292スキル)を同梱しており、チームがこれらのツールをゼロから構築する必要がありません。また、プロンプト、フック、MCP設定、シークレットを対象とするAgentShieldスキャンを含み、ECCのワークフローを変更することなく自己ホスト型またはカスタムモデルエンドポイントをサポートします。

ja.fit: ECCは、すでにClaude Codeを標準として使用しており、再利用可能なスキルとセキュリティスキャンを備えた構造化されたツール支援型の開発ワークフローを求めるチームに最も適していると考えられます。文書化されたプラットフォームサポート表では、複数の統合がベータ版、実験的、または説明のみとされ、完全なパリティではないと分類されているため、主に他のハーネスに依存するチームは機能が限定される可能性があります。

content.goal: Context Mode is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server built for AI coding agents. Its documented goal is reducing how much raw tool output — such as file reads, web fetches, and command results — enters the model's context window, while also preserving session state such as edited files and pending tasks across conversation compaction.
content.usage: Claude Code users install it as a plugin with `/plugin marketplace add mksglu/context-mode` followed by `/plugin install context-mode@context-mode`, then restart Claude Code and run the diagnostics command to confirm the install. The documented prerequisite for this plugin path is Claude Code v1.0.33+; other supported clients register the same server as an MCP tool provider instead.
content.pros: The README states that raw command output is processed inside an isolated sandbox subprocess, so only relevant results reach the conversation, with one documented example of a 315 KB session output reduced to about 5.4 KB — roughly a 98% reduction. It also documents no telemetry and no required account, since session data stays local.
content.cons: On platforms without hook support, such as the Antigravity IDE and Zed, the README states that routing enforcement depends on a manually copied instruction file rather than automatic interception, and estimates this reaches only about 60% of the context savings achieved with hooks. The Cursor plugin is also documented as still awaiting marketplace review.

es.goal: Context Mode es un servidor MCP (Model Context Protocol) para agentes de codificación con IA. Según la documentación, su objetivo es reducir la cantidad de salida bruta de herramientas —como lecturas de archivos, solicitudes web y resultados de comandos— que entra en la ventana de contexto del modelo, y a la vez preservar el estado de la sesión, como archivos editados y tareas pendientes, cuando la conversación se compacta.
es.usage: Los usuarios de Claude Code lo instalan como plugin con `/plugin marketplace add mksglu/context-mode`, seguido de `/plugin install context-mode@context-mode`, luego reinician Claude Code y ejecutan el comando de diagnóstico para confirmar la instalación. El requisito documentado para esta vía es Claude Code v1.0.33+; otros clientes compatibles registran el mismo servidor como proveedor de herramientas MCP.
es.pros: El README indica que la salida bruta de comandos se procesa dentro de un subproceso aislado en sandbox, de modo que solo los resultados relevantes llegan a la conversación, con un ejemplo documentado de una salida de sesión de 315 KB reducida a unos 5.4 KB —aproximadamente un 98% de reducción—. También documenta que no hay telemetría ni cuenta requerida, ya que los datos de sesión permanecen locales.
es.cons: En plataformas sin soporte de hooks, como Antigravity IDE y Zed, el README indica que la aplicación del enrutamiento depende de un archivo de instrucciones copiado manualmente en lugar de la intercepción automática, y estima que esto alcanza solo cerca del 60% del ahorro de contexto logrado con hooks. El plugin de Cursor también aparece documentado como pendiente de revisión en el Marketplace.
es.fit: A juzgar por los logotipos de empresas presentados como usuarios, Context Mode parece adecuado tanto para desarrolladores individuales como para equipos de ingeniería que trabajan con clientes de codificación con IA compatibles con MCP —el README documenta soporte para 17 de estos clientes, además de una integración con la pasarela OpenClaw—. Se distribuye bajo la Elastic License 2.0, una licencia de código disponible que prohíbe ofrecerlo como servicio alojado o gestionado.

ja.goal: Context Modeは、AIコーディングエージェント向けのMCP(Model Context Protocol)サーバーです。ドキュメントによると、ファイル読み取りやWeb取得、コマンド実行結果といった生のツール出力がモデルのコンテキストウィンドウに入る量を減らし、会話が圧縮(compaction)された際にも編集中のファイルや進行中のタスクといったセッション状態を保持することを目的としています。
ja.usage: Claude Codeユーザーは `/plugin marketplace add mksglu/context-mode` を実行した後 `/plugin install context-mode@context-mode` でプラグインをインストールし、Claude Codeを再起動して診断コマンドでインストールを確認します。この方法の前提条件はClaude Code v1.0.33+と記載されており、他の対応クライアントは同じサーバーをMCPツール提供者として登録します。
ja.pros: READMEによると、生のコマンド出力は隔離されたサンドボックスのサブプロセス内で処理され、関連する結果のみが会話に渡されます。315KBのセッション出力が約5.4KBに削減された(約98%削減)という事例が文書化されています。また、テレメトリやアカウントを必要とせず、セッションデータはローカルに保持されると記載されています。
ja.cons: Antigravity IDEやZedのようにフック(hook)をサポートしないプラットフォームでは、READMEによるとルーティングの強制は自動的な介入ではなく手動でコピーした指示ファイルに依存しており、フック使用時と比べて約60%のコンテキスト削減にとどまると見積もられています。Cursorプラグインも、マーケットプレイスの審査待ちであると記載されています。
ja.fit: 利用企業として掲示されたロゴから見ると、Context ModeはMCP互換のAIコーディングクライアントを使う個人開発者とエンジニアリングチームの両方に適していると考えられます——READMEは17種類のクライアントとOpenClawゲートウェイ統合への対応を記載しています。Elastic License 2.0(ソース公開型ライセンス)の下で配布されており、ホスト型・マネージド型サービスとして提供することは禁止されています。

content.goal: Ponytail is a skill/plugin for AI coding agents (including Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot CLI) that guides agents to write minimal code by following a documented decision ladder — checking whether code is needed, reusable, or solvable via the standard library, a native platform feature, or an installed dependency — before writing anything new, while explicitly preserving validation, error handling, security, and accessibility.
content.usage: In Claude Code, install by sending `/plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail` and `/plugin install ponytail@ponytail` as two separate prompts. Once active, commands like `/ponytail-review`, `/ponytail-audit`, and `/ponytail lite|full|ultra|off` review diffs for over-engineering or adjust the intensity level.
content.pros: In a documented benchmark using a headless Claude Code session (Haiku 4.5, n=4, 12 feature tasks), Ponytail reportedly cut lines of code by about 54% (up to 94% on some tasks), cost by about 20%, and time by about 27% versus the same agent without the skill, while holding 100% on a separate safety measure.
content.cons: Using the plugin and hook-based install paths (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) requires `node` on the PATH; without it, the skills still work but the always-on activation hooks stay silent instead of running.
content.fit: The project states it works with 20 agents, listing adapters for tools including Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, and Gemini CLI, suggesting it may fit varied AI-agent coding workflows, though documentation notes command support depth differs by host.

content.goal: Worktrunk is a command-line tool for managing git worktrees, built for running multiple AI coding agents (such as Claude Code and Codex) in parallel. It provides three core commands intended to make working with worktrees as straightforward as working with branches.
content.usage: Worktrunk can be installed via Homebrew with `brew install worktrunk && wt config shell install`, or via Cargo with `cargo install worktrunk && wt config shell install` (Windows, Arch Linux, and Conda/Pixi installs are also documented). A typical workflow starts a worktree with `wt switch --create feature-auth`, then inspects worktrees with `wt list`.
content.pros: The README documents features such as hooks for automating setup at various workflow stages, LLM-generated commit messages, a merge workflow that squashes and rebases in one command, an interactive picker with diff/log previews, shared build caches across worktrees, and PR checkout support.
content.cons: Shell integration must be explicitly installed via `wt config shell install` for commands to change directories, and on Windows the `wt` command name conflicts with Windows Terminal's own command, requiring installation as `git-wt` instead unless that alias is disabled.
content.fit: Worktrunk appears best suited for developers who run several AI coding agents in parallel using git worktrees and want a CLI to reduce the manual steps git worktree normally requires; it documents support for macOS, Linux, Windows, and Arch Linux.

content.goal: HyperFrames is an open-source (Apache 2.0) framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos, usable locally through a CLI, through AI coding agent skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows.
content.usage: Agents typically install the core skill set with `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`, while manual use starts a project with `npx hyperframes init my-video`, then previews and renders it with `npx hyperframes preview` and `npx hyperframes render` to produce an MP4 locally.
content.pros: HyperFrames compositions are authored as plain HTML with data attributes rather than React, rendering is deterministic so identical input yields the same output, the CLI is non-interactive by default for agent workflows, and the project ships 20 packaged skills plus a components catalog covering common needs like captions, charts, and transitions.
content.cons: Running HyperFrames locally requires Node.js 22+ and FFmpeg as prerequisites, and cloning the full repository for development additionally requires Git LFS, since the golden regression-test baselines add roughly 240 MB of .mp4 files that must be fetched separately.
content.fit: Based on its HTML-first, agent-friendly design and deterministic rendering, HyperFrames seems best suited to developers and AI agents automating CI or pipeline video generation, whereas teams already committed to Remotion's React-based authoring model may find switching authoring paradigms less straightforward.

zh-CN.pros: 项目以带数据属性的普通 HTML 而非 React 编写合成内容,渲染被描述为确定性的(相同输入产生相同输出),CLI 默认非交互式,便于代理工作流,并附带 20 个技能以及涵盖字幕、图表、转场等常见需求的组件目录。
zh-CN.cons: 在本地运行需要 Node.js 22 及以上版本和 FFmpeg 作为前置条件,若为开发目的克隆完整仓库,还需要额外安装 Git LFS,因为回归测试基准文件(.mp4)总计约 240MB。
zh-CN.fit: 基于其 HTML 优先、对代理友好的设计以及确定性渲染,HyperFrames 看起来更适合需要在 CI 或流水线中自动生成视频的开发者和 AI 代理,而已经采用 Remotion 的基于 React 创作模式的团队可能需要额外的迁移成本。

es.goal: HyperFrames es un framework de código abierto (Apache 2.0) que convierte HTML, CSS, medios y animaciones navegables (seekable) en videos MP4 deterministas, utilizable localmente mediante la CLI, a través de habilidades para agentes de codificación con IA, o como núcleo de renderizado detrás de flujos de creación alojados.
es.usage: Los agentes suelen instalar el conjunto principal de habilidades con `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`, mientras que el uso manual comienza un proyecto con `npx hyperframes init my-video` y luego lo previsualiza y renderiza localmente con `npx hyperframes preview` y `npx hyperframes render`.
es.pros: Las composiciones se escriben como HTML plano con atributos de datos en lugar de React, el renderizado se describe como determinista (la misma entrada produce la misma salida), la CLI es no interactiva por defecto para flujos con agentes, y el proyecto incluye 20 habilidades junto con un catálogo de componentes para subtítulos, gráficos y transiciones.
es.cons: Ejecutar HyperFrames localmente requiere Node.js 22 o superior y FFmpeg como prerrequisitos, y clonar el repositorio completo para desarrollo requiere además Git LFS, ya que las líneas base de pruebas de regresión suman aproximadamente 240MB de archivos .mp4.
es.fit: Dado su diseño centrado en HTML y amigable con agentes junto con el renderizado determinista, HyperFrames parece más adecuado para desarrolladores y agentes de IA que automatizan la generación de video en CI o canalizaciones, mientras que los equipos ya comprometidos con el modelo de autoría basado en React de Remotion podrían enfrentar una transición menos directa.

ja.goal: HyperFrames は、HTML、CSS、メディア、シーク可能なアニメーションを決定論的な MP4 動画に変換するオープンソース(Apache 2.0)フレームワークで、CLI によるローカル利用、AIコーディングエージェント向けスキルでの利用、あるいはホスト型制作ワークフローのレンダリングコアとしての利用が想定されています。
ja.usage: エージェントは通常 `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes` でコアスキルセットをインストールし、手動利用の場合は `npx hyperframes init my-video` でプロジェクトを作成した後、`npx hyperframes preview` と `npx hyperframes render` でプレビューとローカルでの MP4 レンダリングを行います。
ja.pros: 構成は React ではなくデータ属性付きの通常の HTML として記述され、レンダリングは同一入力から同一出力が得られるという意味で決定論的とされ、CLI はエージェント向けにデフォルトで非対話型であり、字幕・チャート・トランジションなどをカバーする20個のスキルとコンポーネントカタログが付属します。
ja.cons: ローカルでの実行には Node.js 22 以上と FFmpeg が前提条件として必要で、開発用にリポジトリ全体をクローンする場合、回帰テストの基準ファイル(.mp4)が合計で約240MBに達するため、追加で Git LFS のインストールが必要です。
ja.fit: HTML優先でエージェントに配慮した設計と決定論的レンダリングを踏まえると、HyperFrames は CI やパイプラインでの動画生成を自動化する開発者やAIエージェントに適していると考えられる一方、すでに Remotion の React ベースの制作モデルに慣れているチームにとっては移行の手間が伴う可能性があります。

content.goal: MarkItDown is a lightweight Python utility for converting files such as PDF, PowerPoint, Word, Excel, images, audio, HTML, CSV/JSON/XML, ZIP archives, YouTube URLs, and EPubs into Markdown, intended for use with LLMs and related text analysis pipelines.
content.usage: Install with `pip install 'markitdown[all]'` and convert a file from the command line using `markitdown path-to-file.pdf > document.md`. A Python API is also documented via `from markitdown import MarkItDown`, along with optional Azure Document Intelligence or Content Understanding endpoint configuration for cloud-based conversion.
content.pros: The documentation describes support for many file formats, optional dependency groups (e.g. `[pdf]`, `[docx]`, `[pptx]`) for installing only what's needed, and support for 3rd-party plugins such as `markitdown-ocr` that extend functionality without modifying the core repository.
content.cons: The README's Security Considerations section states that MarkItDown performs I/O with the privileges of the current process, similar to `open()` or `requests.get()`, and advises sanitizing inputs and calling narrower `convert_*` functions in untrusted environments, implying that unrestricted use with untrusted input could carry risk.
content.fit: The project is documented as a Python library meant to be incorporated into other systems rather than an end-user application; the contribution scope explicitly excludes web servers, REST/HTTP APIs, hosted conversion services, and desktop/mobile applications, suggesting it fits backend or pipeline integration better than standalone deployment.

content.goal: Humanizer is a Markdown-based skill that rewrites AI-sounding text so it reads as if written by a person, without changing what the text says. According to the README, it works with any agent that supports skills.
content.usage: Install it with the Skills CLI using `npx skills add blader/humanizer --global` for a global install, or omit `--global` for a project-only install; the skill responds to `/humanizer`. On Claude Code 2.1.142 or newer, it can instead be installed as a plugin with `/plugin marketplace add blader/humanizer` and `/plugin install humanizer@humanizer`, responding to `/humanizer:humanizer`. Claude Desktop requires a manual install by downloading the repo as a ZIP or copying SKILL.md into the agent's skill folder.
content.pros: The rewrite process shows its work: an initial draft, a short critique, and a final version. It edits only prose, leaving code, data, frontmatter, and link targets unchanged, and the README states it does not invent facts, asking for missing details instead. It also supports voice matching from a writing sample, and organizes its checks into 25 numbered patterns ordered by strength and frequency.
content.cons: Several patterns are documented as 'weak alone,' meaning they justify an edit only when multiple tells appear together in a passage, since a careful writer may use any one deliberately; this suggests some rewrite decisions may need human judgment in ambiguous cases.
content.fit: This tool appears suited to users of skill-supporting agents such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop who want a documented, pattern-based way to reduce AI-sounding phrasing while preserving factual content; the README does not indicate support for agents lacking skills capability.

es.goal: Humanizer es una skill basada en Markdown que reescribe textos con apariencia de IA para que suenen como si los hubiera escrito una persona, sin cambiar lo que dicen. Según el README, funciona con cualquier agente compatible con skills.
es.usage: Se instala con la Skills CLI mediante `npx skills add blader/humanizer --global` para una instalación global, u omitiendo `--global` para instalarla solo en el proyecto actual; la skill responde a `/humanizer`. En Claude Code 2.1.142 o posterior, también puede instalarse como plugin con `/plugin marketplace add blader/humanizer` y `/plugin install humanizer@humanizer`, respondiendo a `/humanizer:humanizer`. En Claude Desktop se requiere una instalación manual, descargando el repositorio como ZIP o copiando SKILL.md en la carpeta de skills del agente.
es.pros: El proceso de reescritura muestra su trabajo: un borrador inicial, una breve crítica y una versión final. Solo edita la prosa, dejando intactos el código, los datos, el frontmatter y los destinos de los enlaces, y el README indica que no inventa hechos, sino que pregunta cuando falta un detalle. También admite ajustar el tono a partir de una muestra de escritura y organiza sus comprobaciones en 25 patrones numerados por fuerza y frecuencia.
es.cons: Varios patrones están documentados como 'débiles por sí solos', lo que significa que solo justifican una edición cuando varias señales aparecen juntas en un mismo pasaje, ya que un escritor cuidadoso podría usar cualquiera de ellas de forma deliberada; esto sugiere que algunas decisiones de reescritura podrían requerir revisión humana en casos ambiguos.
es.fit: Esta herramienta parece adecuada para usuarios de agentes compatibles con skills, como Claude Code o Claude Desktop, que buscan un método documentado y basado en patrones para reducir el lenguaje con apariencia de IA sin perder el contenido factual; el README no indica compatibilidad con agentes sin soporte de skills.

ja.goal: Humanizerは、内容を変えずにAIらしい文章を人が書いたように書き換えるMarkdownベースのスキルです。READMEによれば、スキルに対応するあらゆるエージェントで利用できます。
ja.usage: Skills CLIを使い、`npx skills add blader/humanizer --global` でグローバルにインストールできます。プロジェクト限定でインストールする場合は `--global` を省略し、スキルは `/humanizer` に応答します。Claude Code 2.1.142以降では、代わりにプラグインとしてインストールでき、`/plugin marketplace add blader/humanizer` と `/plugin install humanizer@humanizer` を実行すると `/humanizer:humanizer` に応答します。Claude Desktopではリポジトリをzipでダウンロードするか、SKILL.mdをエージェントのスキルフォルダに手動でコピーする必要があります。
ja.pros: 書き換え処理は、初稿・簡単な講評・最終版という作業過程を示します。編集対象は文章のみで、コード、データ、フロントマター、リンク先はそのまま保たれ、READMEによれば事実を創作することはなく、不足している詳細があれば代わりに質問します。文章サンプルによる文体マッチングにも対応し、強さと頻度で番号付けされた25のパターンでチェック項目を整理しています。
ja.cons: 一部のパターンは「単独では弱い」と明記されており、これは慎重な書き手が意図的にそのいずれかを使うことがあるため、複数の兆候が同じ箇所にまとまって現れた場合にのみ修正の根拠となることを意味します。このため、曖昧なケースでは一部の書き換え判断に人による確認が必要になる可能性が示唆されます。
ja.fit: このツールは、Claude CodeやClaude Desktopなどスキルに対応するエージェントを利用し、事実関係を保ちながらAIらしい表現を減らすための、文書化されパターンに基づく方法を求めるユーザーに適していると考えられます。READMEはスキル機能を持たないエージェントへの対応については言及していません。

content.goal: This repository catalogs Agent Skills — folders of instructions, scripts, and resources — for use and distribution with the Codex AI agent platform. Skills package capabilities so teams and individuals can complete tasks in a repeatable way.
content.usage: Skills in the `.system` folder install automatically in the latest Codex. Curated or experimental skills are installed via the `$skill-installer` command inside Codex, e.g. `$skill-installer gh-address-comments`, or by specifying a GitHub directory URL: `$skill-installer install https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.experimental/create-plan`. Codex must be restarted afterward for the skill to take effect.
content.pros: Skills are reusable across projects ('write once, use everywhere') and installable with simple named commands through `$skill-installer`. System skills need no manual setup, and the Agent Skills format follows an open standard rather than a proprietary one.
content.cons: The repository is explicitly marked deprecated, with current Codex skill and plugin examples redirected to the openai/plugins repository, so future updates or support for skills here appear uncertain. A Codex restart is also required after each install.
content.fit: This repository likely suits existing Codex users wanting prepackaged, repeatable skills, though given the deprecation notice, those seeking current examples would probably be better served by openai/plugins instead. Licensing is defined per skill in its own LICENSE.txt file.

ko.goal: 이 저장소는 Codex AI 에이전트 플랫폼에서 사용하고 배포하기 위한 Agent Skills(지침, 스크립트, 리소스로 구성된 폴더)를 정리해 놓은 카탈로그입니다. 스킬은 팀과 개인이 특정 작업을 반복 가능한 방식으로 수행할 수 있도록 기능을 패키징합니다.
ko.usage: `.system` 폴더에 있는 스킬은 최신 버전의 Codex에 자동으로 설치됩니다. 큐레이션된 스킬이나 실험적 스킬은 Codex 내부의 `$skill-installer` 명령을 통해 설치하며, 예를 들어 `$skill-installer gh-address-comments`처럼 이름으로 설치하거나 GitHub 디렉터리 URL(`$skill-installer install https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.experimental/create-plan`)을 지정할 수 있습니다. 설치 후에는 Codex를 재시작해야 스킬이 적용됩니다.
ko.pros: 스킬은 여러 프로젝트에서 재사용할 수 있으며('한 번 작성, 어디서나 사용'), `$skill-installer`를 통한 간단한 이름 기반 명령으로 설치할 수 있습니다. 시스템 스킬은 별도의 수동 설정이 필요 없으며, Agent Skills 형식은 독점 방식이 아닌 공개 표준을 따릅니다.
ko.cons: 이 저장소는 명시적으로 더 이상 사용되지 않는(deprecated) 것으로 표시되어 있으며, 현재의 Codex 스킬 및 플러그인 예제는 openai/plugins 저장소로 안내되고 있어, 이 저장소 스킬에 대한 향후 업데이트나 지원 여부는 불확실해 보입니다. 또한 설치할 때마다 Codex를 재시작해야 합니다.
ko.fit: 이 저장소는 이미 Codex를 사용 중이며 미리 패키징된 반복 가능한 스킬을 원하는 사용자에게 적합할 수 있지만, deprecated 표시를 고려하면 최신 예제를 찾는 신규 사용자는 openai/plugins 저장소를 이용하는 편이 더 나을 것으로 보입니다. 라이선스는 스킬마다 개별 LICENSE.txt 파일로 정의되어 있습니다.

es.goal: Este repositorio recopila Agent Skills (carpetas de instrucciones, scripts y recursos) para su uso y distribución con la plataforma de agentes de IA Codex. Las skills empaquetan capacidades para que equipos e individuos puedan completar tareas específicas de forma repetible.
es.usage: Las skills en la carpeta `.system` se instalan automáticamente en la última versión de Codex. Las skills seleccionadas (curated) o experimentales se instalan mediante el comando `$skill-installer` dentro de Codex, por ejemplo `$skill-installer gh-address-comments` por nombre, o especificando una URL de directorio de GitHub como `$skill-installer install https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.experimental/create-plan`. Tras instalar, es necesario reiniciar Codex para que la skill surta efecto.
es.pros: Las skills son reutilizables en distintos proyectos ('escribir una vez, usar en todas partes') y se instalan con comandos simples basados en nombre mediante `$skill-installer`. Las skills del sistema no requieren configuración manual, y el formato Agent Skills sigue un estándar abierto en lugar de uno propietario.
es.cons: El repositorio está marcado explícitamente como obsoleto (deprecated), y los ejemplos actuales de skills y plugins de Codex se redirigen al repositorio openai/plugins, por lo que las futuras actualizaciones o el soporte de las skills aquí parecen inciertos. Además, es necesario reiniciar Codex después de cada instalación.
es.fit: Este repositorio podría ser adecuado para usuarios que ya trabajan con Codex y desean skills reutilizables y preempaquetadas, aunque, dado el aviso de obsolescencia, quienes busquen ejemplos actuales probablemente estarían mejor atendidos por el repositorio openai/plugins. La licencia de cada skill se define individualmente en su propio archivo LICENSE.txt.

ja.goal: このリポジトリは、Codex AIエージェントプラットフォームで使用・配布するためのAgent Skills(指示・スクリプト・リソースを含むフォルダ)をまとめたカタログです。スキルはチームや個人が特定のタスクを再現可能な形で完了できるよう機能をパッケージ化します。
ja.usage: `.system` フォルダ内のスキルは最新版のCodexに自動的にインストールされます。curated(厳選)またはexperimental(実験的)なスキルは、Codex内の `$skill-installer` コマンドを使ってインストールでき、例えば名前指定の `$skill-installer gh-address-comments` や、GitHubディレクトリURLを指定する `$skill-installer install https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.experimental/create-plan` があります。インストール後はスキルを反映させるためにCodexの再起動が必要です。

content.goal: Archify is a Node.js rendering and validation system for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and OpenCode that turns a codebase or system description into a polished, interactive system map directly in chat, using typed JSON IR compiled deterministically into HTML/SVG.
content.usage: Install globally with `npx skills add tt-a1i/archify -g`, then describe a system in agent chat with no repository required. The bundled CLI also supports commands such as `node archify/bin/archify.mjs compare architecture base.json head.json architecture-delta.html --json` for comparing architecture snapshots before merge.
content.pros: It offers five diagram types and four presets with dark/light themes, produces a self-contained HTML file plus PNG, SVG, WebM, and 1200×630 share-card exports, and runs atomic schema, layout, and route validation before delivering output.
content.cons: The README states that automatic Mermaid parsing, general-purpose auto-layout, hosted sharing, and WYSIWYG editing are intentionally outside current scope, so teams needing those capabilities may find the tool insufficient on its own.
content.fit: This appears best suited to teams already using Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI, or OpenCode who want agent-generated, validated architecture diagrams rather than a general-purpose drawing editor; the current development version is v2.17.0-dev.1, released under the MIT license.

es.goal: Archify es un sistema de renderizado y validación en Node.js para Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI y OpenCode que convierte una descripción de código o sistema en un mapa de sistema pulido e interactivo directamente en el chat, usando IR JSON tipado compilado de forma determinista a HTML/SVG.
es.usage: Instálalo globalmente con `npx skills add tt-a1i/archify -g` y luego describe un sistema en el chat del agente, sin necesidad de repositorio. La CLI incluida también admite comandos como `node archify/bin/archify.mjs compare architecture base.json head.json architecture-delta.html --json` para comparar instantáneas de arquitectura antes de una fusión.
es.pros: Ofrece cinco tipos de diagrama y cuatro presets con temas claro/oscuro, genera un archivo HTML autónomo junto con exportaciones en PNG, SVG, WebM y tarjetas para compartir de 1200×630, y ejecuta validaciones atómicas de esquema, diseño y rutas antes de entregar el resultado.
es.cons: El README indica que el análisis automático de Mermaid, el auto-diseño de propósito general, el uso compartido alojado y la edición WYSIWYG quedan intencionalmente fuera del alcance actual, por lo que los equipos que necesiten esas capacidades podrían encontrar la herramienta insuficiente por sí sola.
es.fit: Parece más adecuado para equipos que ya usan Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI u OpenCode y desean diagramas de arquitectura generados por agentes y validados, en lugar de un editor de dibujo genérico; la versión de desarrollo actual es v2.17.0-dev.1, publicada bajo licencia MIT.

content.goal: TradingAgents is a multi-agent LLM-based financial trading framework built with LangGraph. It coordinates specialized agents — fundamentals, sentiment, news, and technical analysts, bullish/bearish researchers, a trader, and a risk-management/portfolio-manager team — to evaluate market conditions and produce trading decisions. The README states the framework is designed for research purposes and is not intended as financial, investment, or trading advice.
content.usage: Install by cloning the repository (`git clone https://github.com/TauricResearch/TradingAgents.git`) and running `pip install .` inside it, optionally in a Python 3.12 virtual environment. Launch the interactive CLI with `tradingagents` (or `python -m cli.main`) to pick tickers, analysis date, LLM provider, and research depth. It can also be used directly in Python via the `TradingAgentsGraph` class and its `.propagate()` method, or run via Docker.
content.pros: The framework supports numerous LLM providers (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, xAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, MiniMax, OpenRouter, Ollama, Azure), works across multiple markets and asset types using Yahoo Finance tickers, and persists a decision log across runs plus offers opt-in checkpoint resume — features that appear to add resilience for longer or repeated analyses.
content.cons: Because output is LLM-driven, two runs on the same ticker and date can differ due to non-deterministic model sampling and live news/social data changing over time; the current curated models are described as reasoning-first and largely ignoring temperature settings, so tighter reproducibility likely requires explicitly selecting a non-reasoning model.
content.fit: The README frames this as a research scaffold for studying multi-agent market analysis rather than a strategy with a fixed, replicable return, suggesting it is best suited to research and experimentation contexts rather than production trading decisions.

El README indica que el framework está diseñado con fines de investigación y no pretende ser asesoramiento financiero, de inversión o de trading.
es.usage: Se instala clonando el repositorio (`git clone https://github.com/TauricResearch/TradingAgents.git`) y ejecutando `pip install .` dentro de él, opcionalmente en un entorno virtual de Python 3.12. La CLI interactiva se lanza con `tradingagents` (o `python -m cli.main`) para elegir tickers, fecha de análisis, proveedor de LLM y profundidad de investigación. es.pros: El framework admite numerosos proveedores de LLM (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, xAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, MiniMax, OpenRouter, Ollama, Azure), funciona en múltiples mercados y tipos de activos usando tickers de Yahoo Finance, y conserva un registro de decisiones entre ejecuciones además de ofrecer reanudación mediante checkpoints opcional, lo que parece aportar mayor resiliencia para análisis largos o repetidos.
es.cons: Dado que la salida depende de un LLM, dos ejecuciones con el mismo ticker y fecha pueden diferir debido al muestreo no determinista del modelo y a datos de noticias/redes sociales que cambian con el tiempo; los modelos actuales seleccionados se describen como orientados al razonamiento y en gran medida ignoran la configuración de temperatura, por lo que lograr mayor reproducibilidad probablemente requiera elegir explícitamente un modelo sin razonamiento.
es.fit: El README presenta esto como una base de investigación para estudiar el análisis multiagente de mercados, no como una estrategia con un rendimiento fijo y replicable, lo que sugiere que es más adecuado para contextos de investigación y experimentación que para decisiones de trading en producción.

content.goal: Claude Plugins — Community is documented as a read-only mirror of the community plugin marketplace for Claude Cowork and Claude Code. The .claude-plugin/marketplace.json file lists plugins available for installation, synced nightly from Anthropic's internal review pipeline.
content.usage: Plugins can be installed from claude.com/plugins/ for Claude Cowork, or through the Claude Code CLI, which requires first adding the marketplace and then installing a specific plugin by running `claude plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-community` followed by `claude plugin install <plugin-name>@claude-community`.
content.pros: Every listed plugin has passed automated security scanning and been approved for distribution before appearing in the marketplace. Submissions go through a single, centralized intake point at clau.de/plugin-directory-submission rather than ad hoc channels.
content.cons: Because the marketplace list syncs only nightly from an internal pipeline, the visible plugin set may lag behind the actual review state by up to a day; exact update timing and discrepancy handling are not detailed in the source material.
content.fit: This repository appears suited for users who want to browse and install pre-vetted plugins through the documented web interface or CLI, rather than contribute code directly, since pull requests opened against the repo are closed automatically.

content.cons: Because each plugin targets a distinct third-party service or tool with its own manifest and likely its own authentication requirements, adopting multiple plugins may involve separate per-service setup; the README does not detail these individual configuration steps.
content.fit: This repository appears best suited for teams and developers already using the Cursor platform who want to extend it with additional developer-tool or SaaS integrations, rather than as a standalone application.

content.goal: awesome-gpt-image-2 is a prompt-engineering repository built around GPT-Image2, offering an "industrial prompt engine" and template library. It documents 544 reverse-engineered cases plus reusable templates, aiming to turn prose-style prompts into structured, composable protocols for batch and automation-friendly image generation, including a GPT Image 2.5 spotlight section.
content.usage: Users can browse the case gallery and templates directly on GitHub, or explore the companion site at https://gpt-image2.canghe.ai. To add the bundled Agent Skill, run `npx skills add freestylefly/awesome-gpt-image-2 --skill gpt-image-2-style-library --agent claude-code codex --global --yes --copy`, or inside Claude Code run `/plugin marketplace add freestylefly/awesome-gpt-image-2`.
content.pros: The repository organizes 544 cases into clear categories (UI, posters, branding, photography, and more) alongside matching prompt templates, and ships an installable Agent Skill compatible with Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor, plus a visual website for side-by-side prompt comparison.
content.cons: Enabling the companion website's paid generation and billing features requires configuring numerous Vercel environment variables (Supabase, Stripe, Google Analytics) and applying multiple Supabase SQL migrations in sequence, an operational setup that goes beyond simply browsing the static prompt library.
content.fit: The structured, template-based approach seems best suited to users building repeatable or automated image-generation workflows with agent tools rather than one-off casual prompting, though effectiveness depends on access to the underlying GPT-Image2 model.

content.goal: OpenViking is presented as an open-source context database for AI agents, giving them a place to store knowledge, remember users, and reuse experience across sessions. It organizes this context as a virtual filesystem reachable through a viking:// URI scheme, browsable with commands such as ls, tree, read, and write.
content.usage: Installation starts with `pip install openviking --upgrade`, then `openviking-server init` configures provider and model settings before the server is started. Users then rely on the bundled `ov` CLI to import and search resources, for example adding a GitHub repository and running semantic queries against it. It requires Python 3.10+ and access to an embedding model plus a VLM, cloud-hosted or local.
content.pros: According to the project's benchmark report, an OpenViking 0.3.22 evaluation found three agent integrations rising from 24–57% to 80–83% accuracy on the LoCoMo memory benchmark, while input tokens dropped 34.3–91.0% and query latency dropped 58.45–66.10%. On tau2-bench, task success rose by +6.87pp (retail) and +11.87pp (airline) versus the same LLM without memory. These figures come from the specific models and setups tested and may not generalize to every configuration.
content.cons: Running OpenViking requires Python 3.10+ plus access to both an embedding model and a VLM, cloud-hosted or local, before the server will start. The core project is released under AGPLv3, and documentation advises configuring authentication before exposing a deployed server beyond localhost.
content.fit: The open-source server can be self-hosted under AGPLv3 with no activation key, suiting teams building agent integrations that need persistent, cross-session memory. Organizations wanting managed hosting or distributed production deployments can instead choose the Managed SaaS or license-key-based Self-Managed (BYOC) commercial editions; the companion desktop console remains in beta for macOS and Windows x64.

ko.goal: OpenViking은 AI 에이전트를 위한 오픈소스 컨텍스트 데이터베이스로 소개되며, 지식을 저장하고 사용자를 기억하며 세션 간에 경험을 재사용할 수 있는 공간을 제공합니다. 컨텍스트는 viking:// URI 체계를 통해 접근하는 가상 파일시스템으로 구성되며, ls, tree, read, write와 같은 명령으로 탐색할 수 있습니다.
ko.usage: 설치는 `pip install openviking --upgrade`로 시작하며, 이후 `openviking-server init`으로 공급자와 모델 설정을 구성한 뒤 서버를 실행합니다. 이후 사용자는 번들로 제공되는 `ov` CLI를 사용해 GitHub 저장소 같은 리소스를 가져오고 시맨틱 검색을 수행할 수 있습니다. 실행을 위해서는 Python 3.10 이상과 임베딩 모델 및 VLM(클라우드 또는 로컬)에 대한 접근이 필요합니다.
ko.pros: 프로젝트의 벤치마크 보고서에 따르면, OpenViking 0.3.22 평가에서 세 가지 에이전트 통합의 LoCoMo 메모리 벤치마크 정확도가 24–57%에서 80–83%로 상승했고, 입력 토큰은 34.3–91.0%, 쿼리 지연시간은 58.45–66.10% 감소했습니다. tau2-bench에서는 메모리가 없는 동일 LLM 대비 작업 성공률이 소매 부문에서 +6.87pp, 항공 부문에서 +11.87pp 상승했습니다. 이 수치는 테스트된 특정 모델과 설정에서 나온 것으로, 모든 구성에 그대로 일반화되지 않을 수 있습니다.
ko.cons: OpenViking을 실행하려면 Python 3.10 이상과 임베딩 모델 및 VLM(클라우드 또는 로컬) 접근이 모두 필요하며, 이러한 조건이 갖춰져야 서버가 시작됩니다. 핵심 프로젝트는 AGPLv3 라이선스로 배포되며, 문서에서는 서버를 로컬호스트 외부에 노출하기 전에 인증을 구성할 것을 권장합니다.
ko.fit: 오픈소스 서버는 AGPLv3 라이선스로 활성화 키 없이 자체 호스팅할 수 있어, 세션 간 지속적인 메모리가 필요한 에이전트 통합을 구축하려는 팀에 적합해 보입니다. 관리형 호스팅이나 분산 프로덕션 배포가 필요한 조직은 대신 매니지드 SaaS 또는 라이선스 키 기반의 Self-Managed(BYOC) 상용 에디션을 선택할 수 있으며, 함께 제공되는 데스크톱 콘솔은 macOS와 Windows x64에서 아직 베타 단계입니다.

zh-CN.goal: OpenViking 被介绍为面向 AI 智能体的开源上下文数据库,为其提供存储知识、记住用户并在会话之间复用经验的场所。其上下文以 viking:// URI 方案组织成虚拟文件系统,可通过 ls、tree、read、write 等命令浏览。
zh-CN.usage: 安装从 `pip install openviking --upgrade` 开始,随后运行 `openviking-server init` 配置提供方与模型设置,再启动服务器。之后可使用随附的 `ov` CLI 导入并搜索资源,例如导入 GitHub 仓库并执行语义查询。运行需要 Python 3.10 及以上版本,并需要访问嵌入模型和 VLM(云端或本地)。
zh-CN.pros: 根据项目的基准测试报告,OpenViking 0.3.22 版本的评测显示,三种智能体集成在 LoCoMo 记忆基准上的准确率从 24–57% 提升到 80–83%,输入 token 减少 34.3–91.0%,查询延迟降低 58.45–66.10%。在 tau2-bench 中,相较于没有记忆的同一大模型,零售场景任务成功率提升 +6.87pp,航空场景提升 +11.87pp。这些数字来自测试所用的特定模型与配置,未必能推广到所有场景。
zh-CN.cons: 运行 OpenViking 需要 Python 3.10 及以上版本,并同时具备嵌入模型与 VLM(云端或本地)的访问权限,服务器才能启动。核心项目采用 AGPLv3 许可证发布,文档建议在将服务器暴露到本地主机之外前先配置身份验证。
zh-CN.fit: 开源服务器可在 AGPLv3 许可证下自行托管,无需激活密钥,适合希望构建具备跨会话持久记忆的智能体集成的团队。需要托管服务或分布式生产部署的组织,则可以选择 Managed SaaS 或需要许可证密钥的 Self-Managed(BYOC)商业版本;配套的桌面控制台目前在 macOS 与 Windows x64 上仍处于测试(beta)阶段。

es.goal: OpenViking se presenta como una base de datos de contexto de código abierto para agentes de IA, que les ofrece un lugar donde almacenar conocimiento, recordar a los usuarios y reutilizar experiencia entre sesiones. Organiza ese contexto como un sistema de archivos virtual accesible mediante un esquema de URI viking://, navegable con comandos como ls, tree, read y write.
es.usage: La instalación comienza con `pip install openviking --upgrade`, seguido de `openviking-server init` para configurar proveedores y modelos antes de iniciar el servidor. Después, se usa la CLI `ov` incluida para importar y buscar recursos, por ejemplo añadiendo un repositorio de GitHub y ejecutando consultas semánticas. Requiere Python 3.10 o superior, además de acceso a un modelo de embeddings y a un VLM, ya sea en la nube o local.
es.pros: Según el informe de benchmarks del proyecto, una evaluación de OpenViking 0.3.22 mostró que tres integraciones de agentes pasaron de 24–57% a 80–83% de precisión en el benchmark de memoria LoCoMo, con una reducción de tokens de entrada de 34.3–91.0% y de latencia de consulta de 58.45–66.10%. En tau2-bench, la tasa de éxito de tareas subió +6.87pp (minorista) y +11.87pp (aerolíneas) frente al mismo LLM sin memoria. Estas cifras provienen de los modelos y configuraciones concretas evaluadas y podrían no generalizarse a todos los escenarios.
es.cons: Ejecutar OpenViking requiere Python 3.10 o superior, además de acceso tanto a un modelo de embeddings como a un VLM, en la nube o local, antes de que el servidor pueda iniciarse. El proyecto principal se distribuye bajo licencia AGPLv3, y la documentación recomienda configurar la autenticación antes de exponer un servidor desplegado más allá de localhost.
es.fit: El servidor de código abierto puede autoalojarse bajo licencia AGPLv3 sin necesidad de clave de activación, lo que parece adecuado para equipos que buscan construir integraciones de agentes con memoria persistente entre sesiones. Las organizaciones que necesiten alojamiento gestionado o despliegues de producción distribuidos pueden optar en cambio por las ediciones comerciales Managed SaaS o Self-Managed (BYOC), esta última basada en clave de licencia; la aplicación de escritorio complementaria sigue en fase beta para macOS y Windows x64.

ja.goal: OpenVikingは、AIエージェント向けのオープンソースなコンテキストデータベースとして紹介されており、知識を保存し、ユーザーを記憶し、セッションをまたいで経験を再利用する場を提供します。コンテキストはviking:// というURIスキームを介してアクセスする仮想ファイルシステムとして構成され、ls、tree、read、writeといったコマンドで閲覧できます。
ja.usage: インストールは `pip install openviking --upgrade` から始まり、続けて `openviking-server init` でプロバイダーとモデルの設定を行ってからサーバーを起動します。その後、同梱の `ov` CLIを使ってGitHubリポジトリなどのリソースを取り込み、セマンティック検索を実行できます。実行にはPython 3.10以上に加え、埋め込みモデルとVLM(クラウドまたはローカル)へのアクセスが必要です。
ja.pros: プロジェクトのベンチマークレポートによると、OpenViking 0.3.22の評価では、3つのエージェント統合におけるLoCoMoメモリベンチマークの精度が24–57%から80–83%に向上し、入力トークンは34.3–91.0%、クエリの遅延は58.45–66.10%削減されました。tau2-benchでは、メモリなしの同じLLMと比較して、タスク成功率が小売分野で+6.87pp、航空分野で+11.87pp向上しています。これらの数値は評価対象となった特定のモデルと設定に基づくものであり、すべての構成に一般化できるとは限りません。
ja.cons: OpenVikingを実行するには、Python 3.10以上に加え、埋め込みモデルとVLM(クラウドまたはローカル)の両方へのアクセスが必要で、これらが揃わないとサーバーは起動しません。コアプロジェクトはAGPLv3ライセンスで配布されており、ドキュメントではlocalhost以外に公開する前に認証を設定するよう推奨しています。
ja.fit: オープンソース版サーバーはAGPLv3の下でアクティベーションキーなしに自前でホストでき、セッションをまたぐ永続的なメモリを備えたエージェント統合を構築したいチームに適しているとみられます。マネージドホスティングや分散型の本番デプロイを求める組織は、代わりにManaged SaaSやライセンスキー方式のSelf-Managed(BYOC)商用エディションを選択でき、付属のデスクトップコンソールはmacOSおよびWindows x64向けにまだベータ版です。

content.goal: This repository hosts open-source components of the Modular Platform, described as a unified platform for AI development and deployment. It includes the MAX Framework and the Mojo Language, covering the compiler, standard library, accelerator library, inference server, and model pipelines documented in the repo.
content.usage: Getting started with the MAX framework involves the quickstart guide at https://max.modular.com/get-started, used for serving a model. Getting started with Mojo involves the quickstart guide at https://mojolang.org/docs/manual/quickstart/. Contributions to the Mojo standard library, MAX accelerator library, or MAX model architectures should begin by reading CONTRIBUTING.md.
content.pros: The repo lists distinct components: the Mojo compiler, Mojo standard library, MAX accelerator library, an MAX inference server with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Python-based MAX model pipelines, and code examples. It accepts community contributions to the standard library, accelerator library, model architectures, and documentation.
content.cons: Contributions to the Mojo compiler itself are not yet accepted, so external changes there may be limited. MAX usage and distribution follow a separate Modular Community License apart from the repository's Apache License v2.0 license, which could mean users need to review third-party library licenses themselves.
content.fit: Given its coverage of an inference server, model pipelines, and a systems language compiler, the project appears aimed at teams building and deploying AI applications who are comfortable managing multiple licenses and validating third-party dependencies themselves.

content.goal: vphone-cli boots a virtual iPhone using Apple's Virtualization.framework, built on PCC research VM infrastructure. It targets Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 15+ (Sequoia).
content.usage: Install via Homebrew with `brew install zqxwce/tap/vphone-cli`, or build from source by cloning the repo (`git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli.git`) and running the provided setup and build scripts. A virtual iPhone can then be created and started with `vphone-cli vm create myphone -V jb` followed by `vphone-cli vm launch myphone`, which downloads firmware, patches the boot chain, performs a DFU restore, and installs the chosen CFW variant.
content.pros: The `vm create` command automates the entire pipeline from download to first boot in a single step. Five firmware variants (`less` through `exp`) offer graduated levels of security bypass, from mitigation-preserving to full jailbreak with anti-VM-detection patches. A host control socket enables programmatic screenshots, touch, and input for automated or AI-driven testing.
content.cons: Setup requires relaxing macOS SIP and AMFI protections on the host to allow unsigned binaries with private entitlements, a change that likely reduces the host's overall security posture. The documentation also notes a known bug in the `ldid-procursus` tool (up to version 2.1.5-procursus7) that can cause the `cfw install` step to hang with unbounded memory growth, requiring a rebuild from source as a workaround.
content.fit: The tool appears suited to developers and security researchers who need an isolated virtual iPhone environment on Apple Silicon for jailbreak research, firmware patch testing, or automated/AI-driven app testing. It is not intended for use inside a nested virtual machine host, since virtualization-based guest boot cannot nest on such configurations.

ko.goal: vphone-cli는 Apple의 Virtualization.framework와 PCC 리서치 VM 인프라를 이용해 가상 iPhone을 부팅합니다. Apple Silicon Mac에서 macOS 15+ (Sequoia)를 대상으로 합니다.
ko.usage: Homebrew로 `brew install zqxwce/tap/vphone-cli` 명령으로 설치하거나, `git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli.git`로 저장소를 클론한 뒤 제공된 설정·빌드 스크립트를 실행해 소스에서 빌드할 수 있습니다. 이후 `vphone-cli vm create myphone -V jb` 명령으로 가상 iPhone을 생성하고, `vphone-cli vm launch myphone` 명령으로 부팅하면 펌웨어 다운로드, 부트 체인 패치, DFU 복원, 선택한 CFW 변형 설치가 자동으로 진행됩니다.
ko.pros: `vm create` 명령 하나로 다운로드부터 첫 부팅까지 전체 파이프라인이 자동화됩니다. `less`부터 `exp`까지 다섯 가지 펌웨어 변형이 제공되어 보안 완화 수준을 단계적으로 선택할 수 있으며, 호스트 제어 소켓을 통해 스크린샷·터치·입력을 프로그래밍 방식으로 제어할 수 있어 자동화 또는 AI 기반 테스트에 활용할 수 있습니다.
ko.cons: 설정 과정에서 macOS의 SIP와 AMFI 보호 기능을 완화해 서명되지 않은 바이너리와 비공개 엔타이틀먼트를 허용해야 하며, 이는 호스트의 전반적인 보안 수준을 낮출 수 있는 것으로 보입니다. 또한 문서에는 `ldid-procursus` 도구(2.1.5-procursus7 이하 버전)의 알려진 버그로 인해 `cfw install` 단계가 멈추고 메모리 사용량이 무한정 증가할 수 있다는 점이 언급되어 있으며, 이를 해결하려면 소스에서 다시 빌드해야 합니다.
ko.fit: Apple Silicon 환경에서 격리된 가상 iPhone이 필요한 개발자나 보안 연구자에게 적합해 보이며, 탈옥 연구, 펌웨어 패치 테스트, 자동화·AI 기반 앱 테스트 등에 활용될 수 있습니다. 다만 가상화 기반 게스트 부팅은 중첩될 수 없다고 명시되어 있어, 이미 가상 머신인 호스트 내부에서 사용하기에는 적합하지 않습니다.

zh-CN.goal: vphone-cli 使用 Apple 的 Virtualization.framework 并基于 PCC 研究虚拟机基础设施来启动虚拟 iPhone,面向运行 macOS 15+ (Sequoia) 的 Apple Silicon Mac。
zh-CN.usage: 可以通过 Homebrew 执行 `brew install zqxwce/tap/vphone-cli` 安装,也可以通过 `git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli.git` 克隆仓库后运行随附的安装与构建脚本从源码构建。之后使用 `vphone-cli vm create myphone -V jb` 创建虚拟 iPhone,再用 `vphone-cli vm launch myphone` 启动,该过程会自动完成固件下载、启动链修补、DFU 恢复以及所选 CFW 变体的安装。
zh-CN.pros: `vm create` 命令可将从下载到首次启动的整个流程一步自动化完成。项目提供从 `less` 到 `exp` 共五种固件变体,可分级选择安全绕过程度;主机控制套接字支持以编程方式截图、触摸和输入操作,可用于自动化或 AI 驱动的测试。
zh-CN.cons: 配置过程中需要放宽 macOS 的 SIP 与 AMFI 保护,以允许使用未签名的二进制文件及私有权限(entitlements),这似乎会降低主机的整体安全性。文档还提到 `ldid-procursus` 工具(2.1.5-procursus7 及以下版本)存在一个已知缺陷,可能导致 `cfw install` 步骤卡住并出现内存无限增长的问题,需要从源码重新构建以规避。
zh-CN.fit: 该工具看起来适合需要在 Apple Silicon 上运行隔离虚拟 iPhone 环境的开发者和安全研究人员,可用于越狱研究、固件补丁测试或自动化/AI 驱动的应用测试。由于基于虚拟化的客户机启动无法嵌套,因此不适合在本身已是虚拟机的主机内部使用。

es.goal: vphone-cli arranca un iPhone virtual usando Virtualization.framework de Apple, sobre infraestructura de VM de investigación PCC. Está dirigido a Mac Apple Silicon con macOS 15+ (Sequoia).
es.usage: Se puede instalar con Homebrew mediante `brew install zqxwce/tap/vphone-cli`, o compilar desde el código fuente clonando el repositorio con `git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli.git` y ejecutando los scripts de configuración y compilación incluidos. Luego, `vphone-cli vm create myphone -V jb` crea el iPhone virtual y `vphone-cli vm launch myphone` lo arranca, automatizando la descarga del firmware, el parcheo de la cadena de arranque, la restauración DFU y la instalación del CFW elegido.
es.pros: El comando `vm create` automatiza en un solo paso todo el proceso, desde la descarga hasta el primer arranque. Se ofrecen cinco variantes de firmware, de `less` a `exp`, con niveles graduales de omisión de seguridad; además, un socket de control del host permite capturas de pantalla, toques y entradas programáticas, útil para pruebas automatizadas o guiadas por IA.
es.cons: La configuración requiere relajar las protecciones SIP y AMFI de macOS en el host para permitir binarios sin firmar con privilegios (entitlements) privados, lo que probablemente reduce el nivel general de seguridad del sistema. La documentación también menciona un error conocido en la herramienta `ldid-procursus` (hasta la versión 2.1.5-procursus7) que puede hacer que el paso `cfw install` se bloquee con un crecimiento de memoria sin límite, siendo necesario recompilar desde el código fuente como solución.
es.fit: La herramienta parece adecuada para desarrolladores e investigadores de seguridad que necesiten un entorno de iPhone virtual aislado en Apple Silicon, para investigación de jailbreak, pruebas de parches de firmware o pruebas automatizadas/con IA. No parece pensada para usarse dentro de un host que sea a su vez una máquina virtual, ya que el arranque de invitado basado en Virtualization no puede anidarse.

ja.goal: vphone-cliは、AppleのVirtualization.frameworkとPCCリサーチVMインフラストラクチャを用いて仮想iPhoneを起動します。macOS 15+ (Sequoia) を実行するApple Silicon Macを対象としています。
ja.usage: Homebrewで `brew install zqxwce/tap/vphone-cli` を実行してインストールするか、`git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli.git` でリポジトリをクローンし、付属のセットアップおよびビルドスクリプトを実行してソースからビルドできます。その後 `vphone-cli vm create myphone -V jb` で仮想iPhoneを作成し、`vphone-cli vm launch myphone` で起動すると、ファームウェアのダウンロード、ブートチェーンのパッチ適用、DFUリストア、選択したCFWバリアントのインストールが自動的に行われます。
ja.pros: `vm create` コマンド一つで、ダウンロードから初回起動までの全パイプラインが自動化されます。`less` から `exp` まで5種類のファームウェアバリアントが用意されており、セキュリティ回避のレベルを段階的に選べます。さらにホスト制御ソケットによりスクリーンショット・タッチ・入力をプログラムから操作でき、自動化やAI駆動のテストに利用できます。
ja.cons: セットアップでは、署名されていないバイナリと非公開エンタイトルメントを許可するためにホストのSIPとAMFI保護を緩和する必要があり、これによりホスト全体のセキュリティ水準が低下する可能性があると考えられます。ドキュメントには、`ldid-procursus` ツール(2.1.5-procursus7以下)に既知のバグがあり、`cfw install` の段階でメモリが際限なく増加してハングすることがあると記載されており、回避にはソースからの再ビルドが必要です。
ja.fit: Apple Silicon上で隔離された仮想iPhone環境を必要とする開発者やセキュリティ研究者に適していると考えられ、ジェイルブレイク研究、ファームウェアパッチのテスト、自動化・AI駆動のアプリテストなどでの利用が想定されます。Virtualizationベースのゲスト起動はネストできないと明記されているため、それ自体が仮想マシンであるホスト内での利用には向いていません。

content.goal: ai-memory is described as long-term memory for AI coding agents, letting a session started in Claude Code continue in another agent such as OpenAI Codex in the same directory without re-explaining the architecture, failed approaches, or open questions.
content.usage: Quick start uses Docker: run `docker run -d --name ai-memory --restart unless-stopped -p 127.0.0.1:49374:49374 -v ai-memory-data:/data docker.io/akitaonrails/ai-memory:latest` to start the server, then `ai-memory install-mcp --client claude-code --apply` and `ai-memory install-hooks --agent claude-code --apply` to wire in an agent CLI.
content.pros: According to the documentation, its source of truth is plain markdown files in a git-backed wiki, and the default path is said to use zero LLM calls, so capture, search, and handoffs reportedly work without any API key.
content.cons: The documented quick-start default runs with no authentication and binds only to loopback, so exposing the server on a LAN reportedly requires adding a bearer token as an extra step; native Windows support is listed as experimental rather than fully supported.
content.fit: The project appears suited to both a single-user workstation and teams running a shared server, and setup requires Docker/Podman or, on Arch Linux, AUR packages.

es.goal: ai-memory se describe como memoria a largo plazo para agentes de codificación con IA, permitiendo que una sesión iniciada en Claude Code continúe en otro agente, como OpenAI Codex, en el mismo directorio sin reexplicar la arquitectura, los enfoques fallidos ni las preguntas abiertas.
es.usage: El inicio rápido usa Docker: se ejecuta `docker run -d --name ai-memory --restart unless-stopped -p 127.0.0.1:49374:49374 -v ai-memory-data:/data docker.io/akitaonrails/ai-memory:latest` para iniciar el servidor, seguido de `ai-memory install-mcp --client claude-code --apply` y `ai-memory install-hooks --agent claude-code --apply` para conectar la CLI del agente.

content.goal: Apache Maka (Incubating) is presented as a high-performance agent workspace that keeps a complete, append-only record of everything it does, via a RuntimeEvent log capturing model messages, tool calls, and permission decisions. The README states results are benchmarked against other harnesses on the same model with an official verifier, with per-task results published in `docs/eval/`.
content.usage: To build from source: `git clone https://github.com/apache/maka.git`, then `npm ci` and `npm run dev` to start the Desktop dev environment with HMR. Stated requirements are Node.js 22.19+ (CI uses Node.js 24), npm 11, Git, and ripgrep; Direct Peer/Peer Mesh development additionally needs Rust stable 1.98+.
content.pros: According to the README, the RuntimeEvent log is the authoritative runtime record rather than just the UI or next prompt, sessions/settings/run records stay local while users supply their own model (cloud API, local model, or gateway), and Desktop, TUI/CLI, and Eval share a single Runtime Host execution authority.
content.cons: The README notes Apache Maka has not made an official Apache release yet, so no signed source archive currently exists as the release artifact. It also states the project is under ASF incubation and active development, so data formats, CLI commands, and experimental capabilities may still change.
content.fit: Based on the stated Desktop Nightly platform support (signed macOS Apple Silicon/Intel builds; unsigned Windows x64 and Linux x64/arm64 previews) and the explicit note that Nightly builds are not intended for production use, this suggests best fit for developers and testers building or evaluating agent harnesses locally.

es.usage: Para compilar desde el código fuente: `git clone https://github.com/apache/maka.git`, luego `npm ci` y `npm run dev` para iniciar el entorno de desarrollo de Desktop con HMR. es.pros: Según el README, el registro RuntimeEvent es el registro autoritativo de ejecución y no solo una proyección de la UI o del siguiente prompt; las sesiones, configuraciones y registros de ejecución permanecen locales mientras el usuario aporta su propio modelo (API en la nube, modelo local o gateway compatible); y Desktop, TUI/CLI y Eval comparten una única autoridad de ejecución (Runtime Host).

es.fit: Dado el soporte de plataformas indicado para Desktop Nightly (compilaciones firmadas para macOS Apple Silicon/Intel; vistas previas sin firmar para Windows x64 y Linux x64/arm64) y la nota explícita de que las compilaciones Nightly no están pensadas para producción, esto parece adecuado sobre todo para desarrolladores y testers que construyan o evalúen harnesses de agentes de forma local.

content.goal: TimesFM is a pretrained time-series foundation model developed by Google Research for time-series forecasting, described in an ICML 2024 paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10688). The latest version, TimesFM 3.0, adds native multivariate forecasting and support for past-only and past-and-future covariates.
content.usage: Install with pip install timesfm[torch] (or pip install timesfm[mlx] for Apple silicon), or run git clone https://github.com/google-research/timesfm.git for a local install. The README shows Python examples using the google/timesfm-3.0-pytorch checkpoint via TimesFM3Evaluator and ModelConfig for univariate and multivariate forecasting.
content.pros: TimesFM 3.0 is documented as ranking #1 on the fev-bench, TIME Benchmark, and GIFT-Eval time-series foundation model benchmarks, and supports flexible covariate-based forecasting without per-task tuning.
content.cons: TimesFM 3.0 pretrained weights are distributed under a separate license, timesfm-non-commercial-license-v1.0, restricted to non-commercial, non-production use, so commercial or production use of the default weights is not permitted; source code and weights up to version 2.5 remain Apache-2.0.
content.fit: This project appears suited to researchers and developers exploring time-series forecasting, including multivariate and covariate-based use cases, though commercial or production deployments would likely need to account for the non-commercial licensing of the TimesFM 3.0 weights, and the repository states it is not an officially supported Google product.
